name: RESIST
fullName: Remote Ischemic Conditioning for Acute Stroke: The RESIST Randomized Clinical Trial
population: n=1500, Median 71 y; 591 (41%) women, NIHSS Not reported in the abstract — patients were enrolled prehospital on symptoms alone, before any diagnostic imaging, Prehospital stroke symptoms for less than 4 h
finding: DID NOT meet: median mRS 2 (IQR 1-3) with RIC vs 1 (IQR 1-3) with sham — RIC was not associated with improved functional outcome
teachingPoint: Ambulance-initiated remote ischemic conditioning does not improve 90-day outcome and is not a prehospital intervention to adopt.

name: RICAMIS
fullName: Effect of Remote Ischemic Conditioning vs Usual Care on Neurologic Function in Patients With Acute Moderate Ischemic Stroke: The RICAMIS Randomized Clinical Trial
population: n=1893, Mean 65 y (SD 10.3); 606 (34.1%) women, NIHSS Acute moderate ischaemic stroke (the trial's severity band; the abstract does not give the numeric NIHSS range or median), Randomised within 48 h of symptom onset
finding: MET: mRS 0-1 in 582 (67.4%) with RIC vs 566 (62.0%) with usual care — an absolute difference of 5.4 percentage points
teachingPoint: Shows a 5.4-point absolute gain in excellent outcome with RIC in moderate stroke, but from an unblinded usual-care comparison the authors themselves say needs replication.

name: SERIC-EVT
fullName: Remote ischaemic conditioning improves outcomes of ischaemic stroke treated by endovascular thrombectomy: the SERIC-EVT trial
population: n=498, Not reported in the abstract, NIHSS Not reported in the abstract, After endovascular thrombectomy for acute large-vessel occlusion
finding: MET: mRS 0-2 in 61.1% with RIC vs 48.9% with sham RIC — note that the effect estimate reported in the abstract is UNADJUSTED
teachingPoint: The first sham-controlled evidence that RIC after thrombectomy may improve 90-day independence — promising enough to justify confirmatory trials, not enough to change practice.

name: EnTRIPS
fullName: Remote Ischemic Postconditioning in Endovascular Thrombectomy for Stroke: The EnTRIPS Randomized Clinical Trial
population: n=270, Mean 65.5 y (SD 16.8); 171 (63.8%) men, NIHSS Not reported in the abstract, Presentation within 24 h of onset; conditioning randomised and started within 6 h AFTER endovascular treatment
finding: DID NOT meet: mRS 0-2 in 81/133 (60.9%) with RIPC vs 78/135 (57.8%) with control — no significant improvement in 90-day functional outcome
teachingPoint: Ultra-early remote ischemic postconditioning after successful thrombectomy was safe but showed no functional benefit, so the RIC-after-EVT question remains open rather than answered.
